- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 1–2% for 30-day horizon.
- After a price spike, model tends to overshoot and then overcorrect; apply a dampening factor (e.g., 0.95) to subsequent forecast steps following a +5%+ increase.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 1–3% per step until convergence.
- Sentiment history is uniformly 0.00 — no behavioral signal — so ignore sentiment-based adjustments; treat all forecasts as purely technical.
- Forecast error is most pronounced in the first 5–7 days of the 30-day window; apply a smoothing filter (e.g., 3-point moving average) to early forecast values.
- If true outcome shows a sharp downward trend after a peak, model often fails to recognize it; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% per day for 3–5 days following a peak.
